items.originalTitle: Bank of America resets Oracle price target – sees 80% upside
items.originalSummary: On Tuesday, October 20, Bank of America (NYSE: BAC ) reviewed its outlook for Oracle (NYSE: ORCL ) and seemingly came to the exact same conclusion as in early June – that the stock is set for a major rally. Specifically, BofA analyst Tal Liani published a note rating ORCL shares as a ‘Buy’ and estimating they will soar 80.83% from their press time price of $132.72 to $240 within the next 12 months. Notably, the Wall Street expert first made this forecast early in June when Oracle stock was changing hands at roughly $206 and only started the descent that took it, by press time on October 20, 35.51% lower. At the time, BofA cited the technology giant’s $50 billion equity and debt raises as factors reducing concerns regarding the firm’s data center buildout, as well as the broader software sector strength. In July, Oracle’s credit rating was downgraded to BBB – – one step above ‘junk’ – and the most recent developments threaten to degrade it even further. Additionally, the company issued a force majeure notice for its New Mexico data center in late September, though Oracle claimed the decision represents a relatively commonplace move and is unremarkable . Such notices are usually issued to protect firms in case of massive disruption, such as wars or natural calamities. Elsewhere, despite appearing exceedingly bullish given the recent developments, BofA’s latest Oracle stock price target is slightly below the Wall Street average. Indeed, ORCL shares are, overall, considered a ‘Strong Buy’ and boast twenty-seven positive, four ‘Hold’, and one ‘Sell’ recommendation, per the data Finbold retrieved from TipRanks on Tuesday, October 20. The average price target is likewise bullish and estimates that ORCL equity will soar 87.68% to $249.11 in the next 12 months. Still, October revisions were generally more conservative. Out of the three provided since the month started, only BofA opted for a ‘Buy’ recommendation, while RBC Capital’s Matthew Hedberg and Dan Ives – perhaps the biggest technology bull on Wall Street – rated the shares as ‘Neutral’.

items.summary: Bearish investors accumulated roughly $32 billion in paper profits over seven days as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped over 12% during an eight-session slump. Broad market indexes felt the ripple effect, with the S&P 500 on track for its worst weekly decline since June and the Nasdaq 100 sliding 5%. Short sellers betting against AI cloud provider CoreWeave Inc. netted more than $1 billion in mark-to-market profits following distressed debt signals and rising default risks.

items.title: 特斯拉獲利聚焦 SpaceX 合併討論。這是分析師馬斯克的說法。
items.originalTitle: Tesla Earnings Spotlight SpaceX Merger Talk. Here's What Analysts, Musk Say.
items.originalSummary: Ahead of earnings, investors are invited to submit questions for the call. One entry that got a lot of upvotes was about timing for a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla, Musk's automaker. Musk's companies have had business and financial relations for years, even sharing personnel and some board members. Tesla invested $2 billion into xAI, which later converted into shares of SpaceX. The AI unit of SpaceX also spent about $430 million last year on Tesla's Megapacks, which are battery energy storage systems, and $143 million on Cybertrucks. With SpaceX hitting the public market in June, speculation about a more permanet tie-up has been swirling. SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell told CNBC ahead of the IPO that a merger "might make Elon's life a little easier." A demo of Tesla's next-generation Roadster last week stirred up further merger excitement among Musk fans. The new Roadster was developed with SpaceX and incorporates its technology, including cold gas thrusters, to enable the car to launch, hover and flip in mid-air. —Lora Kolodny

investorBrief.event: 在財報公佈之前，投資人受邀在電話會議上提出問題。特斯拉向 xAI 投資了 20 億美元，後來轉換為 SpaceX 的股票。 SpaceX 的人工智慧部門去年也在特斯拉的 Megapack（電池儲能係統）上花費了約 4.3 億美元，在 Cyber​​truck 上花費了 1.43 億美元。新款 Roadster 是與 SpaceX 合作開發的，並採用了其技術，包括冷氣體推進器，使汽車能夠在半空中發射、懸停和翻轉。
investorBrief.why: 這會直接影響市場對未來營收、EPS 與估值的預期。投資上比已公布的單季數字更重要的是公司接下來的財測方向、毛利與需求能見度。
investorBrief.stance: 在財報公佈之前，投資人受邀在電話會議上提出問題。獲得大量支持的一篇文章是關於 SpaceX 和馬斯克的汽車製造商特斯拉之間潛在合併的時機的。馬斯克的公司多年來一直保持著業務和財務關係，甚至是共享人員和一些董事會成員。特斯拉向 xAI 投資了 20 億美元，後來轉換為 SpaceX 的股票。 SpaceX 的人工智慧部門去年也在特斯拉的 Megapack（電池儲能係統）上花費了約 4.3 億美元，在 Cyber​​truck 上花費了 1.43 億美元。隨著 SpaceX 於 6 月上市，有關更永久合作關係的猜測一直在流傳。

items.originalTitle: Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ:CBRS) Stock Gets Price Target Cut from TD Cowen
items.originalSummary: Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) shares fell 3.46% to $116.48 in premarket trading Tuesday, extending losses one day after TD Cowen sharply cut its price target for the artificial intelligence chipmaker while maintaining a Buy rating. TD Cowen lowered its 12-month target to $175 from $275 in a research note issued before Monday’s market open. The $100 reduction represents a 36.4% cut. The revised target is $34 below the $209 minimum recorded in an October 5 analyst survey compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence, although it remains approximately 50% above Tuesday’s premarket share price. TD Cowen was among the bookrunners for Cerebras’ May initial public offering , which was priced at $185 per share. Its latest target is $10 below that offering price.

historyItems.originalTitle: AstraZeneca and Oracle launch global AI collaboration to advance clinical trial optimisation and support better patient outcomes
historyItems.originalSummary: Partnership aims to advance solutions to improve care pathways, clinical trial matching, safety monitoring, and guideline-directed care AstraZeneca and Oracle Health and Life Sciences today announced a unique collaboration to leverage AstraZeneca's scientific, clinical development and regulatory expertise with Oracle's real-world data, cloud infrastructure, and AI-enabled clinical capabilities to accelerate clinical research and bring evidence-driven insights into care workflows to accelerate clinical trial optimisation and help more patients receive the right care sooner. Many serious conditions are diagnosed late; patients can wait a long time before they are referred and there are gaps in how we translate scientific advancements into clinical practice. This collaboration is designed to test practical ways to connect scientific research directly to clinical workflows and transform care. Initial areas of exploration include clinical trial recruitment, earlier diagnosis, drug-safety monitoring and leveraging real-world evidence across the lifecycle of a medicine. Programmes will span AstraZeneca's core disease areas including oncology, cardiovascular, renal and metabolic diseases, respiratory and immunology, and rare disease. The collaboration will span multiple international projects with key regions including the US, Middle East, and Europe working with local governments and within applicable regulations to ensure these could be scaled in the future. The first programme will focus on supporting hypertension care and clinical research in Abu Dhabi, in partnership with healthcare company, M42. This will help clinical teams identify patients with uncontrolled hypertension; implementing guideline-directed care; and improving the recruitment for clinical trials. Pascal Soriot, Chief Executive Officer, AstraZeneca said: "This unique collaboration brings leaders in healthcare and AI together at a global scale to accelerate the journey from the discovery of medicine to patient care. Combining AstraZeneca's world class science with Oracle's deep data and technology expertise, we can help clinicians identify patients sooner, optimise clinical trials, and generate evidence continuously across the lifecycle of a medicine." Mike Sicilia, chief executive officer, Oracle said: "Some of the most important opportunities for AI are in healthcare, where better use of data can help turn scientific innovation into better outcomes for patients. By bringing AstraZeneca's scientific expertise together with Oracle's data, cloud, AI, and healthcare capabilities, we have an opportunity to help accelerate research, connect more patients to clinical trials, and ultimately bring relevant insights into care faster." Anne-Claire Gerbaldi, Chief Digital, Data and AI Officer, AstraZeneca, said: "Too many patients are diagnosed late or face a long journey to get the care they need. historyItems.originalTitle: CoreWeave stock attempts to rebound on Goldman Sachs upgrade to Buy
historyItems.originalSummary: CoreWeave ( CRWV ) shares rose 3% before surrendering their gains Monday after Goldman Sachs upgraded the neocloud provider to Buy from Neutral. The analyst also raised the stock's price target from $106 to $139 per share following a sell-off of more than 25% last week. A viral chart showing CoreWeave's spiking bond yields last week underscored concerns about the company's debt-heavy balance sheet and whether it can scale its business quickly enough to cover rising interest expenses.

historyItems.originalTitle: Test: The 2026 Ford F-150 STX Lobo Fails to Impress for the Money
historyItems.originalSummary: Ford makes the long haul and enters Grasso’s Garage with an aesthetically pleasing and proven F-150 Lobo edition pickup truck that is ready for all consumers. With a 600-mile range on a full tank, our F-150 Lobo tester offers an upgraded 5.0-liter Coyote V-8 engine packed with 400 horsepower and 410 lb.-ft. of torque. Paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission, the F-150 Lobo gets up and goes and is smooth. Wrapped in Oxford White, the Lobo package is an additional $4,695 and includes 22-inch gloss black wheels, an electronic locking rear axle and all-season tires. Our STX Series pickup comes with LED fog lights, black cloth interior and a black and dark gray grill. Upgraded options include a tray style floor liner, mobile office package, 36-gallon fuel tank, SiriusXM and spray-in bedliner for a combined additional $2,630 total. While the interior is simple and typical Ford, it serves the consumers well with its 12-inch SYNC4 infotainment system. Rear-view camera and parking sensors, selectable drive modes and a host of safety features came standard on our weeklong tester. Standard warranty is a 3-year / 36,000 mile bumper to bumper, a 5-year / 60,000 mile powertrain, and a 5-year / 60,000 mile roadside assistance.

historyItems.originalTitle: Prediction market odds on Tesla-SpaceX merger are above 50% for early 2027
historyItems.originalSummary: The prediction market odds of a merger between Tesla and SpaceX have risen above 50% for early 2027, according to CNBC. This increase reflects heightened speculation around a possible union of the two companies, both controlled by Elon Musk. Notably, these odds do not stem from any formal announcement or filing, but rather from market activity and sentiment. Recent analyses, including one from Barclays, suggest potential scenarios for a merger, though official confirmations from either company remain absent. Observers should monitor communications from Tesla and SpaceX, particularly any formal disclosures or statements from Elon Musk. An SEC filing or official press release could significantly impact current market pricing. Additionally, regulatory reviews or statements from antitrust authorities may influence the perceived likelihood of a merger. As market participants react to new information, shifts in pricing could further indicate changing expectations.

historyItems.summary: Arista Networks (ANET) 透過新的開放式乙太網路機架規模產品組合將高密度人工智慧基礎設施置於其故事的中心，旨在跨液冷機架連接加速器以處理大規模工作負載。最新的人工智慧機架規模發布是在 Arista Networks 股價強勁上漲後推出的，該股 90 天股價回報率上漲 15.51%，今年迄今上漲 57.84%，而五年內的長期股東總回報率約為 8 倍。截至最後收盤價 210.88 美元，1 天股價回報率下跌 2.70％，儘管 30 天漲幅 5.66％ 和 1 年股東總回報率 43.02％ 表明持續的勢頭，受到先前對 Arista 800G 交換產品的興趣以及對人工智能基礎設施需求日益關注的支持。
historyItems.originalTitle: Arista Networks (ANET) Stock Forecast and Price Target 2026
historyItems.originalSummary: Arista Networks (ANET) has put high-density AI infrastructure at the center of its story with a new open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, aiming to link accelerators across liquid-cooled racks for large-scale workloads. The latest AI rack-scale launch lands after a strong run in Arista Networks' shares, with the stock up 15.51% on a 90-day share price return and 57.84% year to date, while long-term total shareholder return over five years is about 8x. At a last close of US$210.88, the 1-day share price return fell 2.70% even as the 30-day gain of 5.66% and 1-year total shareholder return of 43.02% indicate ongoing momentum, supported by prior interest in Arista's 800G switching products and growing attention on AI infrastructure demand.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Cargo Mission Approaching Station
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX just delivered some surprisingly strange cargo to the International Space Station, including tiny brain models, 3D heart tissue, and technology for making artificial retinas in space. Scientists hope these experiments could unlock new ways to treat devastating brain diseases, restore eyesight, and test future medicines. The shipment also includes materials for creating unusual glass in near weightlessness and the station’s final upgraded solar arrays.

historyItems.originalTitle: Chip-Machine Supplier ASML Boosts Guidance for Third Time on Surging AI Demand
historyItems.originalSummary: By Mauro Orru ASML Holding improved its annual forecasts for the third time this year and said it was looking at ways to boost production of its semiconductor-making machines even more as the race to build artificial-intelligence infrastructure fuels demand for advanced chips. The Dutch group is projecting annual sales between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros, equivalent to a range of $49.27 billion to $50.39 billion, compared with prior guidance of 43 billion euros to 45 billion euros. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched metric of pricing power and profitability--should come in at roughly 56%, compared with a previous guidance range of 54% to 56%. The revisions show how much ASML's fortunes have come to benefit from the build-out of data centers that turned chips into a red-hot commodity. Surging semiconductor demand means that ASML's clients like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics and Intel will need more of its machines so they can produce enough chips. ASML shares in Amsterdam gained more than 2% in European morning trading, consolidating ASML's lead as Europe's most valuable listed company. Its stock is up more than 80% over the past 12 months on a wave of investor fervor around AI and expectations that chips and semiconductor-making tools will remain in high demand for years to come. "Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030," ASML Chief Executive Christophe Fouquet said. AI demand pushed up the cost of certain types of chips as companies hoard semiconductors to power data centers, leading to a supply squeeze. Micron Technology Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said last month that supplies of memory and storage chips would be much tighter in the coming years. In a bid to cash in on that tightness, ASML is seeking to increase production of its deep ultraviolet lithography tools as well as its more advanced extreme ultraviolet systems. In July, it had earmarked a 30% boost in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. However, Fouquet said it was becoming clear that wouldn't be enough to meet demand and that ASML was looking at ways to bolster capacity even more, especially for 2028 and beyond. Earlier this year, ASML executives alluded to the possibility of price increases, saying that a tight chip market gave ASML more negotiating power. Finance chief Roger Dassen said that while the company had now completed conversations with key customers, the effect of higher prices wouldn't show on 2026 figures. "It will start to become visible partly in the course of 2027. The full impact of that you will start to see in 2028 and beyond," he said. ASML posted sales of 11.66 billion euros for the third quarter, up from 7.52 billion euros a year earlier. historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries Gets $21 Billion for Plants in US-Japan Deal
historyItems.originalSummary: GlobalFoundries Inc plans to build two new chip plants with the backing of as much as US$21 billion from the Japanese government, part of an arrangement that also includes the US taking a 4 percent stake in the company. Under an agreement announced on Wednesday, GlobalFoundries will operate factories at its site in upstate New York that are jointly owned by the US and Japan. The facilities will be funded with money from Japan’s pledge to invest US$550 billion in the US. The factories will make so-called essential chips, the vital yet less sophisticated semiconductors used in vehicles, industrial equipment and communications gear. Photo: John Carl D’Annibale, The Albany Times Union via AP The GlobalFoundries agreement is meant to boost American production of essential chips and reduce dependence on East Asian suppliers — addressing a national security concern for the US. Under a broader arrangement with GlobalFoundries, the US Department of Commerce will take a roughly 4 percent equity stake in the company, “further enabling the American public to share in GF’s growth.” GlobalFoundries will get to redirect funds from a previous US CHIPS and Science Act grant to invest in honing its manufacturing abilities. That includes advancing its work in fields such as silicon photonics, chip packaging and silicon germanium. In a separate statement, the US Department of Commerce said it was reallocating US$955 million in CHIPS Act incentives to go toward GlobalFoundries’ factory expansion and modernization. As part of the agreement, the company will devote US$5 billion to capital investments at its plants in New York and Vermont. The new Japan-linked factories will be operated in the same way that GlobalFoundries runs its current facilities, which serve customers such as Apple Inc and Japanese firms including Renesas Electronics Corp. Profits will be divided among the owners and GlobalFoundries, following an approach laid out in last year’s US trade deal with Japan. US President Donald Trump touted the accord on his Truth Social site, saying it would help revitalize America’s industrial base and create jobs.

historyItems.originalTitle: Dell stock plunges 11%, leading data center sell-off as fears mount about 'enterprise AI timing'
historyItems.originalSummary: Dell shares plunged 11% on Wednesday, leading a data center equipment sell-off on mounting concerns that enterprise AI spending will not justify the AI buildout. Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Oracle and Super Micro also declined. Barclays analysts downgraded Dell, HPE and NetApp to the equivalent of hold from buy in a Wednesday report to clients. The analysts cited enterprise AI timing after significant stock gains. Barclays analysts said enterprise spending at Dell, HPE and NetApp had not shown a meaningful acceleration related to AI. The analysts instead attributed increased revenue to the global memory shortage. The analysts noted that infrastructure companies had passed higher memory prices on to customers. Barclays analysts said businesses typically allocate just 5% of IT budgets to AI, despite growing expectations that enterprise AI adoption will drive hardware replacement. The analysts found that only about a quarter of total enterprise AI spending goes toward hardware. The analysts said normalizing and eventually declining memory prices could weigh on infrastructure-related revenue. Data center server and other backend equipment makers have attracted investor interest this year on expectations of large equipment sales linked to AI demand for years ahead. Dell shares have risen more than 300% this year, making Dell one of the market's top performers. HPE shares have risen about 160% this year. NetApp shares have doubled this year. However, sentiment toward AI infrastructure has shifted recently, partly because of concerning revenue figures from OpenAI. Investors also fear that rising interest rates will create difficulties because much of the AI buildout relies on debt. Oracle, a heavy borrower, fell 9% on Wednesday and is now down 33% for the year. Neocloud company CoreWeave plunged 15% on Wednesday, erasing CoreWeave's gains for 2026. Memory is a highly cyclical business. Memory stocks fell this week after China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, also known as CXMT, reported progress over the weekend on a new chip structure. Micron shares are down 11% for the week. South Korea's SK Hynix has fallen 13% in U.S. trading this week. Western Digital has dropped more than 8% this week.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to open 2 new chip plants in New York with $21 billion in financing from Japan
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.summary: Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) 在推出與 NVIDIA 為 MGX 生態系統共同開發的 24 kW 800 V 至 12 V DC-DC 供電板後，將其人工智慧資料中心的雄心作為重點。儘管有英偉達的合作和人工智慧資料中心的推動，納維半導體的股價一直波動不定，在最近的產品消息發布後，其 1 天股價回報率為 4.6％，90 天股價回報率下降了 21.25％，3 年股東總回報率為 76.82％，這表明其長期前景比過去一年的 16.87%。
historyItems.originalTitle: Why Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) Shares Moved After Its Latest Update
historyItems.originalSummary: Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) has put its AI data center ambitions in focus after unveiling a 24 kW 800 V-to-12 V DC-DC power delivery board, co-developed with NVIDIA for the MGX ecosystem. Despite the Nvidia collaboration and AI data center push, Navitas Semiconductor's share price has been choppy, with a 1-day share price return of 4.6% following recent product news, a 90-day share price return down 21.25%, and a 3-year total shareholder return of 76.82%, which points to a much stronger longer-run story than the 16.87% decline over the past year.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to Build Two Chip Plants With Up to $21 Billion Funding
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.originalTitle: Palantir and London mayor's office settle lawsuit over UK police contract
historyItems.originalSummary: In the United Kingdom, US technology company Palantir and the office of London Mayor Sadiq Khan have settled the company’s lawsuit over the decision not to approve a contract with London police worth £50 million, or $66 million. Channel NewsAsia reports , citing a joint statement by the parties. Palantir agreed with London police on a two-year contract to use artificial intelligence systems. They were intended to automate some tasks and help analyse evidence. However, London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime refused to approve the agreement. It told police that no open competition had been held for the contract. Reports said that Khan’s representative also expressed concerns that Palantir did not align with London’s values. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . In a joint statement, Palantir and London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime said they had settled the case and withdrawn their mutual allegations. The parties also said that the decision not to enter into the contract was not based on Palantir’s values or ethics, or on broader coverage of the company’s activities. The office said it does not and has never had a policy of refusing to enter into contracts with Palantir. The company may participate in future procurement procedures. The United Kingdom is also reviewing the National Health Service’s £330 million contract with Palantir. A parliamentary committee said there was a clear mismatch between the company and the United Kingdom’s values and recommended invoking an early termination clause. Louis Mosley, head of Palantir’s UK division, called the recommendation irresponsible.

historyItems.originalTitle: ASML's strong orders ease fears AI spending boom is running out of steam
historyItems.originalSummary: AMSTERDAM, Netherlands: Demand for advanced chipmaking equipment is stretching years into the future, with ASML saying customers are already looking to place orders for 2029 and even 2030 as the artificial intelligence investment boom continues to drive semiconductor expansion. The Dutch company, the world's biggest maker of equipment used to produce AI chips and advanced semiconductors, said October 14 that planned increases in its production capacity for 2027 and 2028 would not be enough to meet demand. ASML said in July that it planned to increase capacity by 30 percent in 2027 and by another 30 percent in 2028. CEO Christophe Fouquet said that the company was now seeing "a lot of order intake for 2028. But also, some strong interest to already place orders for 2029 and sometimes even 2030." The outlook helped ease investor concerns that the surge in spending on AI infrastructure could be approaching a peak. ASML's customers include TSMC, which manufactures chips for Nvidia, as well as Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix and Micron. The companies have been investing heavily to expand chip production. "There were concerns that the AI trade was running out of steam," said Gordon Kerr, European macro strategist at KBRA, adding ASML's results showed "demand for chips remains strong, and infrastructure spending is likely to continue well into 2027". ASML shares rose two percent on October 14. The stock has gained almost 70 percent this year, while the company is Europe's largest by market value at about €586 billion. The company reported third-quarter net profit of 4.96 billion euros on net sales of 11.7 billion euros. It forecast fourth-quarter sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros, or US$15.9 billion to $17 billion. ASML also raised its full-year sales outlook from at least 43 billion euros to 44 billion euros to 45 billion euros.

historyItems.originalTitle: Credo Launches Micro-Emitter Standardization Initiative | Business | Oct 2026
historyItems.originalSummary: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications Joined by Initial Participants Including Leading Hyperscaler and Optical Technology Solution Providers AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC Under the OCP Networking Project Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (Credo) (NASDAQ: CRDO), an innovator in providing connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions, alongside prominent optical technology providers, today announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Among the first to join with Credo include a leading hyperscaler as well as AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC, bringing together expertise spanning the full optical connectivity stack to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012753816/en/ Credo, alongside prominent optical technology providers, has announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. Micro-emitter technology brings new ways of moving volumes of data, while dramatically improving reliability, power efficiency, and bandwidth density. Arrays of micron-scale light sources make up the transmit side of an optical link. Rather than pushing a few optical channels to extreme data rates, many micro-emitters operate in parallel at optimal individual speeds, enabling layer zero redundancy to improve reliability. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. The specification, targeted for OCP approval in 2027, will address requirements for link power, efficiency, signaling, parallelism, physical form factors – including module and connector footprint, link budget, and compliance. By defining specifications, the SRMO Workstream aims to give data center operators, hyperscalers, and system designers access to a broad ecosystem of interoperable components with supply chain resiliency, accelerating time to deployment and fostering continued innovation in optical connectivity. “As AI workloads scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accelerators, the industry needs a standardized approach to wide, parallel optical connectivity — not a patchwork of components that do not fit together or interoperate,” said L.K. historyItems.originalTitle: Department of Commerce Announces Agreement with GlobalFoundries to Amend Its Existing CHIPS Program Award and Reallocate $955 Million to Accelerate Investments in Silicon Photonics, Silicon-Germanium, and Advanced Packaging
historyItems.originalSummary: Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Program Office has agreed with GlobalFoundries to amend its existing award and reallocate up to $955 million in incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act. The amendment will increase the portion of an existing CHIPS Program award allocated to GlobalFoundries’ modernization and expansion of its semiconductor manufacturing facilities in Malta, NY and Burlington, VT. As part of the amendment, GlobalFoundries has agreed to expand its capital investment in these facilities to $5 billion. The total amount of the existing CHIPS Program award will not be increased. The investment will expand domestic manufacturing capacity for technologies increasingly critical to communications infrastructure and data centers, including silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and the first U.S.-based source of silicon interposers supporting advanced packaging technologies. “GlobalFoundries is expanding its investment to develop and manufacture critical semiconductor technologies enabling data center and high-performance compute infrastructure,” said Bill Frauenhofer, Executive Director for Semiconductor Innovation and Investment at the Department of Commerce. “The CHIPS Program award supports GlobalFoundries efforts to onshore and accelerate the development of these important semiconductor components." GlobalFoundries is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling technologies from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GlobalFoundries delivers differentiated, power efficient, and high-performance solutions for automotive, aerospace and defense, data center, smart mobile devices, internet of things and other high growth markets. historyItems.originalTitle: Coherent (COHR) Stock Looks About Right Following Sold Out Capacity News
historyItems.originalSummary: Coherent has become one of the most prominent optical hardware stories in the market. After a very steep multi year climb, the key question is whether the current share price lines up with what its earnings can reasonably support. Over the past 3 years the stock has returned about 7x, which places significant emphasis on the idea that its profit power can eventually catch up with that move. Recent headlines around sold out optical capacity into 2029 and tighter supply for certain data center components may support expectations for stronger earnings and cash generation over time, but they also raise the stakes if those hopes do not materialize. Your read on Coherent is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Coherent's shares could be worth .

historyItems.title: 為什麼 AST SpaceMobile 股票持續下跌
historyItems.summary: AST SpaceMobile 合作夥伴 Ligado 敦促 FCC 仔細審查 Rocket Lab 提出的 80 億美元收購 Iridium 的提議。 Ligado 援引了 SpaceX 的指控，稱 Iridium 在八個月內提交了 50 多份拒絕申請。 Neutron 的首次亮相已推遲到 2027 年，而 Iridium 收購仍計劃在 2027 年中期完成。 Rocket Lab (RKLB) 的股價上週暴跌超過 25%，因為其上市計畫再次被推遲。 Neutron 火箭對該股造成重創，而 AST SpaceMobile 的頻譜合作夥伴 Ligado Networks 對其提議以 80 億美元收購 Iridium Communications 的競爭優勢提出質疑。 RKLB 股票週五收在 50.84 美元，當日下跌近 8%。
historyItems.originalTitle: Why AST SpaceMobile Stock Keeps Falling
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile partner Ligado urged the FCC to scrutinize Rocket Lab’s proposed $8 billion Iridium acquisition.Ligado cited SpaceX’s allegation that Iridium filed more than 50 petitions to deny over eight months.Neutron’s debut has slipped into 2027, while the Iridium acquisition remains targeted for a mid-2027 close.Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB) plunged over 25% last week as another delay to its Neutron rocket battered the stock, while AST SpaceMobile’s spectrum partner Ligado Networks challenged the competitive benefits of its proposed $8 billion acquisition of Iridium Communications.RKLB stock closed Friday at $50.84, down nearly 8% for the session. The decline extended its losing streak to eight sessions, wiping out 38% of its value since its Oct.7 close. The selloff deepened after Rocket Lab pushed Neutron’s debut into 2027. Ligado Takes Aim At Iridium DealIn a recent letter to the FCC, Ligado accused Iridium of using regulatory proceedings to delay competing satellite services, including Ligado’s proposed SkyTerra Next offering with AST SpaceMobile.Iridium has long used the FCC’s procedures as an anticompetitive weapon,” Ligado’s lawyers said.“While Rocket Lab and Iridium tout MSS competition as the core public interest benefit of the acquisition, Iridium’s own conduct suggests its modus operandi at the FCC for decades has been to suppress rather than promote competition,” Ligado said.Ligado asked the FCC to scrutinize the transaction’s incentives and public-interest benefits, particularly if Iridium does not withdraw filings that Ligado characterizes as attempts to cause delay.AST SpaceMobile Plans Fuel Spectrum FightLigado’s commercial interest runs directly through SkyTerra Next, a proposed mobile satellite service using AST SpaceMobile’s low-Earth-orbit constellation to support direct-to-device connectivity.Ligado alleges that Iridium has opposed the service to protect its existing business. It argues that SkyTerra Next would compete with Iridium without creating an interference risk. The letter also points to Iridium’s previous interest in accessing Ligado’s spectrum. According to Ligado, the FCC rejected the move, after which Iridium continued pursuing objections concerning potential interference. Ligado said that the acquisition could reinforce those incentives by increasing the importance of protecting the strategic value of Iridium’s L-band spectrum.“Accordingly, we urge the Commission to carefully scrutinize the transaction to ensure that the parties’ intent and incentives align with the public interest,” its lawyers said.SpaceX’s Objections Enter Deal FightLigado also drew on SpaceX’s earlier criticism of Iridium, citing an August filing accusing the operator of repeatedly attempting to impede competitors. “Iridium exploits Commission procedure to deny or delay its competitors from providing better service to millions of American consumers, businesses, and first responders,” SpaceX said in the filing quoted by Ligado.According to Ligado’s letter, SpaceX documented more than 50 petitions to deny filed by Iridium over an eight-month period. historyItems.originalTitle: Oracle Proposes Plan that could deliver at least $155M to offset customers utility costs in New Mexico
historyItems.originalSummary: Austin, Texas-Oct 13, 2026 Oracle today announced a proposed Energy Service Agreement with El Paso Electric (EPE) for Project Jupiter to support late-stage construction, initial commissioning, emergency backup power at the site and to meet life safety needs for New Mexican workers at the data center. As indicated earlier this year, the primary power source for Project Jupiter will continue to be provided by the Bloom Energy fuel cell microgrid. There is no change to our plan. As part of the Energy Service Agreement, Oracle expects to pay $10 million for power annually for 10 years even if its usage is below contracted levels. This agreement helps offset shared electric system costs that would otherwise be borne by EPE's New Mexico customers and supports affordable electric rates. In addition, a separate agreement includes a proposal to provide as much as $55 million annually in direct credits for up to three years for EPE's New Mexico residential and small business customers. This credit could begin benefiting customers in 2027. "We welcome the opportunity to facilitate Oracle's credit to further affordability for our customers," said Kelly Tomblin, president and CEO of El Paso Electric. "Growth and investment in New Mexico has always been an EPE priority and we support the effort Oracle is making to ensure that this growth benefits our residential and small commercial customers." Earlier this year, Oracle signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge and made a commitment to pays its own way for energy and infrastructure costs. The proposed agreements with El Paso Electric not only ensure that Oracle pays for the energy costs, but it also supports affordable rates and additional offset of energy costs for its neighbors. "We realize the impact that electric rate increases have on the community and our proposed solution takes that burden off of New Mexico ratepayers," said Mahesh Thiagarajan, executive vice president, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. "We're taking this action now - well before our data center comes online - to deliver a direct, meaningful benefit to New Mexico households and small businesses and help ensure the community shares in the value created by Project Jupiter." Additional information will be provided following the filing of the Energy Service Agreement. historyItems.originalTitle: Mainspring Energy Signs Landmark 1.6 GW Agreement with AEP for Reliable, Affordable Power Capacity
historyItems.originalSummary: Agreement accelerates adoption of Mainspring's Linear Generators at grid scale in the rapidly growing market for onsite power generation MENLO PARK, Calif., Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mainspring Energy, Inc. has signed a landmark sales agreement with American Electric Power (AEP), one of North America's largest electric utilities, to provide up to 1.6 gigawatts (GW) of Mainspring Linear Generators through 2034. As part of the agreement, AEP purchased its first tranche of the Mainspring products, at 190 megawatts (MW), for delivery beginning in 2027.

historyItems.originalTitle: Is Applied Materials (AMAT) A Bargain Following Its EPIC Center Launch?
historyItems.originalSummary: Applied Materials (AMAT) just cut the ribbon on its EPIC Center in Sunnyvale, a US$5b semiconductor R&D hub that pulled the stock into focus after a modest premarket pullback. For investors, the near term has been choppy for Applied Materials, with the share price down 1.87% over the last session and 8.25% over the week. However, that pullback sits against a sharp year-to-date share price gain of 85.04% and a 1-year total shareholder return of 127.94%, which points to strong longer term momentum even as sentiment cools ahead of earnings and as the EPIC Center and recent AI-focused partnerships reset expectations around future opportunity and risk.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Lifts Off for Thursday Cargo Delivery
historyItems.originalSummary: NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). The spacecraft lifted off from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral, Florida, at 06:33 a.m. local time (1:33 p.m. Moscow time/10:33 a.m. GMT) on the 35th resupply mission to the orbital station. Cargo Dragon will transport more than 2.8 tons of cargo to the orbiting outpost, including equipment for scientific experiments studying the effects of microgravity on heart tissue, as well as a set of solar arrays for the ISS. The spacecraft is expected to dock automatically with the ISS on October 15. In mid-November, Cargo Dragon is scheduled to return to Earth carrying the results of scientific experiments and equipment for repair.

historyItems.summary: 休斯頓 (CW39)——週四，NASA 的 SpaceX 龍飛船與國際太空站對接，執行補給任務。週二，龍飛船搭載獵鷹 9 號火箭從卡納維拉爾角發射升空，為國際太空站運送了超過 6,300 磅的物資和硬件，包括新的科學實驗、貨物以及運往軌道實驗室的最後一對國際太空站滾動太陽能電池陣。最後一對太陽能電池陣列將完成太空站電力系統的增強，增加用於研究、操作和太空站安全、受控脫軌的可用電力。太空人將在計劃於今年秋天晚些時候進行的一系列太空行走中安裝這些陣列。
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Counts Down to Launch for Station Resupply Mission
historyItems.originalSummary: HOUSTON (CW39) — NASA’s SpaceX resupply mission aboard a Dragon spacecraft docked with the International Space Station on Thursday. The Dragon spacecraft, which launched from Cape Canaveral on Tuesday aboard a Falcon 9 rocket, is carrying more than 6,300 pounds of supplies and hardware for the ISS, including new scientific experiments, cargo, and the final pair of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays to the orbiting laboratory. The final pair of solar arrays will complete the space station’s power system augmentation, boosting available electricity for research, operations, and the station’s safe, controlled deorbit. Astronauts will install the arrays during a series of spacewalks planned for later this fall. The Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the space station until mid-November when it will depart and return to Earth with time-critical research and cargo, splashing down off the coast of California.

historyItems.originalTitle: How to Invest In SpaceX (SPCX) — And How Not To
historyItems.originalSummary: Space Exploration Technologies is seeking FAA approval, via a new Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement, to lift Starship activity at Boca Chica from the current 25 launches to a potential ceiling of 456 launches and 912 landings a year, while scaling Starship landing and expenditure sites globally. In the same period, SpaceX has committed nearly US$8b to acquire 800 MHz of mobile spectrum and has secured FCC clearance for up to 15,000 direct-to-cellphone Starlink satellites, which moves the business toward a capital-intensive role as both global carrier and high-cadence launch operator. The focus now shifts to how Space Exploration Technologies' investment narrative incorporates this capital-heavy Starlink Mobile and Starship expansion.

historyItems.originalTitle: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications - Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd
historyItems.originalSummary: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications Joined by Initial Participants Including Leading Hyperscaler and Optical Technology Solution Providers AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC Under the OCP Networking Project Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (Credo) (NASDAQ: CRDO), an innovator in providing connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions, alongside prominent optical technology providers, today announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Among the first to join with Credo include a leading hyperscaler as well as AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC, bringing together expertise spanning the full optical connectivity stack to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012753816/en/ Credo, alongside prominent optical technology providers, has announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. Micro-emitter technology brings new ways of moving volumes of data, while dramatically improving reliability, power efficiency, and bandwidth density. Arrays of micron-scale light sources make up the transmit side of an optical link. Rather than pushing a few optical channels to extreme data rates, many micro-emitters operate in parallel at optimal individual speeds, enabling layer zero redundancy to improve reliability. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. The specification, targeted for OCP approval in 2027, will address requirements for link power, efficiency, signaling, parallelism, physical form factors – including module and connector footprint, link budget, and compliance. By defining specifications, the SRMO Workstream aims to give data center operators, hyperscalers, and system designers access to a broad ecosystem of interoperable components with supply chain resiliency, accelerating time to deployment and fostering continued innovation in optical connectivity. “As AI workloads scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accelerators, the industry needs a standardized approach to wide, parallel optical connectivity — not a patchwork of components that do not fit together or interoperate,” said L.K. Bhupathi, Associate Vice President

historyItems.summary: 多倫多，2026 年 10 月 12 日 (環球通訊社) -- 資料中心基礎設施和先進技術解決方案領域的全球領導者 Celestica Inc.（紐約證券交易所代碼：CLS）（多倫多證券交易所代碼：CLS）今天推出了 Celestica DS6005，這是一款共同安全性封裝 (CPO) 數據驅動器 (CPO) 數據交換中心，旨在滿足寬帶、低位數據 (CPO) 數據組件和新功率的系統要求。 DS6005 基於 Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson 交換器晶片構建，旨在以專為 OCP ORv3 機架設計的緊湊 1.5OU 外形尺寸提供高達 102.4Tbps 的交換容量。
historyItems.originalTitle: Celestica Introduces the DS6005 Data Center Switch with Co-Packaged Optics to Enable Power-Efficient AI Fabrics
historyItems.originalSummary: TORONTO, Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Celestica Inc. (NYSE: CLS) (TSX: CLS), a global leader in data center infrastructure and advanced technology solutions, today introduced the Celestica DS6005 , a co-packaged optics (CPO) data center switching system designed to address the bandwidth density, power, latency, and reach requirements of next-generation AI data center networks. Built on the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 – Davisson switch chip, the DS6005 is designed to deliver up to 102.4Tbps of switching capacity in a compact 1.5OU form factor designed for OCP ORv3 racks. By co-packaging optical engines with the switch ASIC, the DS6005 eliminates the need for traditional front-panel pluggable optics, helping data center operators optimize bandwidth density, reduce latency, and improve power efficiency in the AI data center. “AI infrastructure is driving unprecedented demand for bandwidth, while power, thermal management, latency, and reach are becoming increasingly important constraints,” said Gavin Cato, SVP & GM Portfolio Solutions & AI Platform Engineering, Celestica. “The DS6005 brings co-packaged optics, liquid cooling, field-replaceable external laser modules, and CPO-aware software management together in a compact platform designed to help customers build scalable and power-efficient AI fabrics.” Purpose-built to support AI/ML scale up and scale out networking, the DS6005 is a fully liquid-cooled, co-packaged optics data center switch that slashes power consumption and improves cluster efficiency while lowering latency and increasing reliability for next-generation AI clusters.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX stock poised for a catalyst-fueled 2027
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX ( SPCX ) isn't going quietly into what could be an eventful 2027. Elon Musk's rocket business said late last week it acquired a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio . It positions Musk's satellite business, Starlink, to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US. Shares of AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ) tanked on the news on Friday. Meanwhile, SpaceX is reportedly seeking to raise $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia chips. "The debate is whether a company this early in its public life should carry that much leverage," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said. "We think the contracted backlog in AI and the cash generation of Starlink give SpaceX the capacity to service it, and we would rather see this compute financed and deployed than deferred."

historyItems.originalTitle: Microchip Expands Data Center Portfolio to Meet Evolving AI Infrastructure Demands
historyItems.originalSummary: CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As AI workloads drive demand for more scalable and flexible data center architectures, organizations are looking for faster, more efficient ways to move, store and protect data. Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) is helping to address these needs by expanding its portfolio of data center solutions with new innovations in PCIe ® connectivity, NVMe ® storage and acceleration that support high-performance computing infrastructure. "Customers are looking for technology partners that can address multiple challenges across the infrastructure stack while helping simplify design and accelerate deployment,” said Brian McCarson, corporate vice president and GM of Microchip’s data center solutions business unit. “By continuing to expand our portfolio, we're providing the building blocks needed to create more efficient, secure and adaptable platforms for today’s increasingly distributed and data-intensive computing environments.” Designed to bring PCIe Gen 6 connectivity to space- and power-constrained platforms, the Switchtec™ PCIe 6.0 Low-Lane-Count (LLC) switch provides up to 64 PCIe Gen 6 lanes, 32 ports and flexible x2, x4, x8 and x16 bifurcation options. Integrated Direct Memory Access (DMA) supports efficient peer-to-peer data movement between connected devices while reducing host CPU involvement. Like Microchip’s larger Switchtec Gen 6 devices, the LLC switch features PCIe Multicast and partitioning capabilities along with robust security through hardware root of trust and secure boot technologies. The new device delivers PCIe Gen 6 capabilities with a smaller, lower power footprint to extend support to a broader range of data center and intelligent edge applications. To address the industry’s requirements for secure, scalable and AI-optimized storage infrastructure, Microchip is updating its Flashtec ® SSD controller portfolio with an enhanced version of the PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 controller. Building on the controller's high-performance, power-optimized architecture, the updated device adds support for Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite (CNSA) 2.0 to help customers prepare for emerging post-quantum security requirements. Dual-port capability enables highly available storage architectures through redundant data paths and load balancing, while advanced virtualization, Quality of Service (QoS) management and flexible programmability help optimize performance. Together, these enhancements extend the Flashtec platform’s ability to address evolving NAND technologies, high-capacity SSD designs and next-generation enterprise, hyperscale and AI deployments. Microchip is also expanding the capabilities of its Adaptec ® SmartRAID 4300 family of NVMe RAID storage accelerators with a series of enhancements designed to address practical operational needs. The updates are focused on strengthening storage security, minimizing downtime, expanding data protection and simplifying deployment across a wider range of environments. historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia to start dealing out GPUs in high-stakes AI-RAN gamble
historyItems.originalSummary: Some drivers are happy to run a car until the chassis has corroded and the engine coughs with every agonizing change of gear. Others less constrained by economic circumstances want a new vehicle every time the paint is nicked. Many big telcos currently seem to have more in common with the first group, determined to run their mobile networks until the basestations are shrouded in cobwebs. Any upgrades, including to 6G, should not have to require hardware replacement, they are telling vendors. Yet Nokia wants to sell them a completely new engine. The Finnish company has publicly teamed up with Nvidia to design radio access network (RAN) products built on the giant chipmaker's graphics processing units (GPUs). It has stopped developing new custom silicon with partner Marvell Technology, although it will continue to support its existing 4G and 5G range for years. Ultimately, however, customers will have to buy new hardware to enjoy new features. There is no guarantee the situation will be all that different for customers of Ericsson. Operators using its purpose-built 5G products today may need to invest in newer application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) to support forthcoming 5G-Advanced and 6G software. But Nokia's GPU strategy is undoubtedly much riskier. While commonplace in data centers and certain gadgets, Nvidia's chips have never been used for RAN compute. If telcos balk at the idea, Nokia could be in trouble. "If you don't have a companion strategy that's based on classic ASICs, you really have created jeopardy, I think," said Marcus Weldon, a former Nokia chief technology officer who was also president of its Bell Labs research unit. Yet the rewards could be immense if Nokia can prove that GPUs have advantages over ASICs in the RAN. In recent months, it has argued that its GPU-led strategy will support a doubling in spectral efficiency, among other benefits, by 2028. In a RAN market that is not expected to grow in the next few years, such improvements could justify the initial hardware outlay and even translate into market share gains for Nokia, allowing it to recover 5G ground lost to Ericsson and Samsung. That could be a disaster for Nokia's rivals. Numerous operators are now giving Nokia's AI-RAN products a test drive before they become commercially available early next year. None has yet said anything in public about the initial experience, and many operators have previously voiced concern about using what is still perceived to be a very expensive and energy-hungry chip in the RAN. Overkill has been the word on some lips, as if putting a GPU in the RAN is like using a rocket launcher to kill a rat. But Nokia has been advertising a slimline GPU that could be slotted into an existing Airscale chassis originally designed to support Marvell Technology's silicon. It will have to function with the same power constraints and be available for the same price, according to executives. They have also promised it will support software upgrades and new AI algorithms for years – unlike any ASIC. historyItems.originalTitle: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Stock Falls After AI Revenue Reset Shakes Demand Outlook
historyItems.originalSummary: Advanced Micro Devices (NasdaqGS:AMD) came under pressure after OpenAI sharply cut its revenue outlook, triggering a broad AI sell-off. AI hardware suppliers with close ties to OpenAI, including AMD, were among the most heavily traded stocks following the revision. The reset in OpenAI's revenue expectations has prompted investors to reassess demand assumptions for AMD's AI accelerators and infrastructure projects. OpenAI's revenue reset and the resulting AI stock pullback deserve to be weighed against the rest of our AMD findings. Our analysis turns up 3 other big wins for Advanced Micro Devices as well. For readers looking beyond AMD and OpenAI to other ways of getting exposure to the AI theme, start with 38 AI small caps .

historyItems.originalTitle: Intel and Applied Materials Just Deepened Their AI Partnership. Which Stock Looks Better Positioned?
historyItems.originalSummary: Applied Materials Inc. (NASDAQ: AMAT ) and Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC ) announced on October 6 that they are expanding their partnership on next-generation AI chipmaking. The two will work together on transistors, the wiring that connects them, and advanced packaging. That includes Intel's Foveros technology for stacking chips in 3D. Teams will work out of Applied's EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel's research campus in Oregon. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the goal is to move new technology from the lab into high-volume U.S. production faster. The Intel deal adds another dimension to Applied Materials' growth story. But before judging AMAT by its valuation, see what Jim Cramer thinks investors may be missing .

historyItems.originalTitle: FormFactor (FORM) Stock Could Be 33% Undervalued After AI Testing News
historyItems.originalSummary: FormFactor (FORM) has been dropped from the S&P 600 and added to the S&P 400, a reshuffle that shifts the semiconductor tester into the mid cap index universe. The reshuffle lands on a stock that has already been very active, with FormFactor's 1 month share price return of 22.32% and year to date share price return of 135.97% pointing to strong momentum even after a 6.36% drop over the past week. At a latest share price of $139.67, that move sits on top of a 1 year total shareholder return of 266.20%. This builds on multi year total shareholder returns above 280% and indicates that investors have been steadily marking up both growth potential and risk appetite around the stock.

historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry, and AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon stocks are getting crushed
historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is moving past satellite internet, and it’s making a big move into the US wireless market. The company has agreed to buy cellular spectrum licences from investment firm Grain Management in a deal reportedly worth about $8 billion, its biggest move yet to compete with established mobile carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, according to a WSJ report . The deal is for spectrum in the 800MHz band, which is for mobile services delivered via terrestrial infrastructure such as cell towers, not satellites. If the acquisition is approved, SpaceX could combine those airwaves with its growing Starlink satellite network to create a more comprehensive wireless service. SpaceX has already been rolling out Starlink in areas beyond the usual broadband. The company has been working with T-Mobile for over a year to offer basic wireless connectivity in remote areas. SpaceX is also launching newer Starlink satellites that are capable of carrying more data. The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch up to 15,000 satellites dedicated to mobile services. Add a developer who says he vibe-coded replacements for seven of the company’s apps, and the triumphant headline practically writes itself. Adobe can presumably start clearing its desk. AI chatbots have quietly become a go-to source for medical advice the extent that some are dangerously skipping real doctors. But when AI's health advice goes wrong, doctors may never see the exchange behind it. Researchers from Binghamton University, Stanford, Texas A&M, and Indiana University published a paper in Nature Health examining what happens after a chatbot gives you bad health information. Their biggest concern is not just that chatbots can be wrong. It is that those mistakes often leave no trace for doctors, researchers, or regulators to catch.

historyItems.summary: 馬斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 正在超越衛星互聯網，並大舉進軍美國無線市場。根據《華爾街日報》報道，該公司已同意從投資公司 Grain Management 購買蜂窩頻譜許可證，據稱這筆交易價值約 80 億美元，這是該公司迄今為止與 AT&T、Verizon 和 T-Mobile 等老牌行動營運商競爭的最大舉措。該協議涉及 800MHz 頻段的頻譜，該頻段用於透過蜂窩塔等地面基礎設施提供的行動服務，而不是衛星。如果收購獲得批准，SpaceX 可以將這些無線電波與其不斷發展的 Starlink 衛星網路結合起來，創造更全面的無線服務。
historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry and stocks like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are getting crushed
historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is moving past satellite internet, and it’s making a big move into the US wireless market. The company has agreed to buy cellular spectrum licences from investment firm Grain Management in a deal reportedly worth about $8 billion, its biggest move yet to compete with established mobile carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, according to a WSJ report . The deal is for spectrum in the 800MHz band, which is for mobile services delivered via terrestrial infrastructure such as cell towers, not satellites. If the acquisition is approved, SpaceX could combine those airwaves with its growing Starlink satellite network to create a more comprehensive wireless service. SpaceX has already been rolling out Starlink in areas beyond the usual broadband. The company has been working with T-Mobile for over a year to offer basic wireless connectivity in remote areas. SpaceX is also launching newer Starlink satellites that are capable of carrying more data. The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch up to 15,000 satellites dedicated to mobile services. Leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI companies are reportedly preparing for a potential AI disaster that could turn the public against artificial intelligence. According to an Axios report, industry leaders are privately running through possible scenarios for what happens after a catastrophic AI incident. What kind of AI disaster are companies preparing for? AI is a useful tool for handling many tasks in private as well as professional settings, but medical advice, especially diagnosis, is one area where I generally draw the line. General-purpose chatbots tend to sound confident and convincing while giving medical advice, even when they are wrong, as studies have previously found. That being said, Google's new research points to a much more convincing use for AI in healthcare. Its Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer chatbot, or AMIE for short, could help prepare both sides before the appointment even begins.

historyItems.title: TELUS 整合進度導致 AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 估值可能被低估 67%
historyItems.summary: 在公司和 TELUS 完成首次整合測試後，AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 重新成為人們關注的焦點，該測試將 TELUS 的地面無線網路與 AST SpaceMobile 的衛星系統連接起來，在加拿大提供智慧型手機直接到衛星服務。 AST SpaceMobile 與 TELUS 的整合取得進展是在該公司股票經歷波動之後，該公司股價在過去一天下跌了 6.13%，在過去一個月下跌了 13.90%，導致今年迄今為止下跌了 31.80%。與上市初期相比，三年和五年的長期股東總回報仍然非常高，這表明近期的疲軟反映了風險預期的變化，而不是更廣泛的多年走勢的簡單逆轉。
historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) Could Be 67% Undervalued On TELUS Integration Progress
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) moved back into focus after the company and TELUS completed their first integration test connecting TELUS' terrestrial wireless network with AST SpaceMobile's satellite based system for direct smartphone to satellite service in Canada. AST SpaceMobile's integration progress with TELUS comes after a volatile run for the stock, with the share price falling 6.13% over the past day and 13.90% over the past month, contributing to a 31.80% decline in the year to date. Long term total shareholder return over three and five years remains very large compared with the initial listing period, suggesting recent weakness reflects shifting risk expectations rather than a simple reversal of the broader multi year move.

historyItems.originalSummary: President Trump says Americans should "buy a Dell," but his brokerage account sold between $500,001 and $1 million of Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) stock on Aug. 21, according to a federal ethics disclosure made public on Oct. 8.
